newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tribasa to bid on Mexico's Pacific-North rail line.
newsitem.headline: Tribasa to bid on Mexico's Pacific-North rail line.

text.p: Mexican construction giant Grupo Tribasa and its partners RailTex Inc and Impulsora Tlaxcalteca de Industrias (Itisa) will bid on Mexico's Pacific-North rail line that is up for privatization, Tribasa said on Friday.

"We are very interested (in the line)," Fernando Gutierrez, Tribasa's vice president for operations, told Reuters. "The Pacific-North is the main route through northwest Mexico, while the Chihuahua-Pacific is a short line."
Tribasa recently withdrew from bidding on the Chihuahua-Pacific line.

The Chihuahua-Pacific line, which runs through the spectacular Copper Canyon that is popular with tourists, is the first of several rail lines to be privatized by the Mexican government. The winner is expected to be announced this month.
The concession for the Pacific-North line, which starts in Colima state state and runs toward the U.S. border, is due to be awarded next April or May.
